quantities.period: Applications received on or after 12 December 2025; May 2026 process
quantities.qualifier: at least; new transmission applications within stated date scope
quantities.excerpt: new transmission-system applications of at least 1 MVA
quantities.context:
<!-- D17 -->
Ireland provides a concrete continuing obligation. EirGrid's May process implements the regulator's policy for new transmission-system applications of at least 1 MVA received on or after 12 December 2025. Under that process, nominated generation must remain operational and meet the specified relationship between de-rated export capacity and the datacentre's maximum import capacity. If that generation fails or is withdrawn, a credible plan for immediate replacement is required; otherwise import capacity may be reduced or disconnected. Continuing renewable compliance is also required. The regulator's wider policy differentiates requirements by project size. The May document records pending judicial review proceedings concerning the underlying policy and warns that their outcome could change the process. Their subsequent outcome is unverified here. These are inspected process provisions, not verified outcomes for a particular customer's agreement. [EirGrid process, PDF pages 3 to 5 and 8](https://cms.eirgrid.ie/sites/default/files/publications/Data-Centre-Connection-Offer-Process-and-Policy-V3-May-2026.pdf#page=4); [CRU decision, size-dependent requirements](https://cruie-live-96ca64acab2247eca8a850a7e54b-5b34f62.divio-media.com/documents/CRU2025236_Large_Energy_User_connection_policy_decision_paper.pdf).

quantities.period: S24: Proposed procurement for the 2028/29 resource adequacy shortfall; January policy origin
quantities.qualifier: initial target, subject to reductions
quantities.excerpt: initial target of 6,831.3MW UCAP, subject to qualifying reductions
quantities.context:
<!-- D19 -->
PJM's US proposals have a different status. Its January policy direction preceded the later auction shortfall. The July Reliability Backstop Procurement filing used an initial target of 6,831.3MW UCAP, subject to qualifying reductions. Its proposed USD555/MW-day UCAP limit applies to the MW-weighted average levelised procurement cost, not every offer. The separate August Interim Resource Adequacy Service proposal drew a Market Monitor protest. The inspected September backstop answer still requested acceptance; final Commission disposition is unverified. These records cannot be presented as an adopted universal connection restriction. [July filing](https://www.pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercDockets/9806/20260731-er26-3380-000.pdf); [Monitor protest](https://www.monitoringanalytics.com/filings/2026/IMM_Protest_Docket_No_ER26-3515_20260903.pdf); [September answer](https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/documents/ferc/filings/2026/20260910-er26-3380-000.pdf).

quantities.period: September 2026 financing announcement
quantities.qualifier: company-reported equity financing, not all assigned to infrastructure
quantities.context:
<!-- D25 -->
Mistral reports a EUR3B Series D led by Samsung in September. It separately describes European Compute Units that exchange multi-year customer commitments for infrastructure access. The inspected material does not assign all equity proceeds to infrastructure or disclose the complete customer contract.
